body:
### Descrição

Este PR entrega a página de **produto individual**, acessada via `slug`, com suporte completo a variações de **pose**, **tamanho**, e integração com o **contexto de carrinho**.  
Também foram realizados ajustes importantes nas rotas de API, geração de dados mockados e persistência no `localStorage`.

---

### ✅ Implementações

---

### 1. 📄 Página de Produto Específico (`[slug]`)

- Criada a rota dinâmica em:  
  `src/app/products/[slug]/page.tsx`
- `getProduct(slug)` consulta a API `/api/products/[slug]`
- Componente `ProductPage` com:
  - Renderização da imagem de acordo com a **pose atual**
  - Botões de seleção de **pose** (relaxado, dormindo, comendo)
  - Botões de seleção de **tamanho** (PP, P, M, G, GG)
  - Botão de "Adicionar ao carrinho" ativado somente após seleção válida

---

### 2. 📦 Dados Mockados com Faker + Seed

- Utilização de `faker.seed(2025)` para garantir:
  - Dados estáveis entre execuções
  - Testabilidade e consistência
- Produtos mockados incluem:
  - `id`, `title`, `slug`, `price`, `pose`
  - `image` no padrão `/assets/pandas/panda-{id}/{pose}.webp`
  - `variations`: tamanhos e poses disponíveis

---

### 3. 🌐 API `/api/products/[slug]`

- Nova função `getMockProductBySlug(slug)` com **cache interno**
- Evita divergência entre produtos da Home e da página individual
- Retorno:
  ```ts
  {
    product: Product;
    success: true;
  }
  ```
- Em caso de erro: resposta 404 ou 500 com mensagem

---

### 4. 🧠 Tipagens

```ts
// types/product.type.ts
export type Product = {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  slug: string;
  price: number;
  image: string;
  description: string;
  featured: boolean;
  pose: string;
  variations: {
    sizes: string[];
    poses: string[];
  };
};

// types/cart.type.ts
export interface CartItem {
  product: Product;
  selectedPose: string;
  selectedSize: string;
  quantity: number;
}
```

---

### 5. 🛒 Contexto do Carrinho

- `addToCart(product, pose, size)` agora exige **pose e tamanho**
- Identificação única por combinação: `id + pose + size`
- Operações adaptadas:
  - `removeFromCart`
  - `updateQuantity`
  - `totalPrice`
- **Persistência com `localStorage`**:
  - Estado salvo automaticamente com `useEffect`
  - Restaurado ao carregar a aplicação

---

### 6. 🔁 Consistência Visual e Persistência

- Preço, título, imagem e pose são **consistentes** em:
  - Página inicial
  - Página de produto
  - Carrinho
- Todos os dados gerados de forma **determinística com seed**

---

### 🔍 O que está validado:

| Elemento                             | Status |
|--------------------------------------|--------|
| Slug único por produto               | ✅     |
| Preço estável entre execuções        | ✅     |
| Dados mockados centralizados         | ✅     |
| API `/products/[slug]` funcional     | ✅     |
| Página de produto interativa         | ✅     |
| Adição ao carrinho com variações     | ✅     |
| Persistência do carrinho (localStorage) | ✅  |

---

## Tipo da Mudança

- [x] Seleção de pose e tamanho opera corretamente  
- [x] Integração com contexto do carrinho válida

- [x] Carrinho persistente entre sessões

- [x] Mensagens de commit seguem o padrão do projeto  

---

### Comentários adicionais

Esta entrega marca a consolidação da estrutura de navegação entre produtos e a maturidade do fluxo de e-commerce com dados estáveis, contexto robusto e API simulada com realismo.

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 snyk Code Injection vulnerability

The package snyk before 1.1064.0 is vulnerable to Code Injection when analyzing a project. An attacker who can convince a user to scan a malicious project can include commands in a build file such as build.gradle or gradle-wrapper.jar, which will be executed with the privileges of the application. This vulnerability may be triggered when running the the CLI tool directly, or when running a scan with one of the IDE plugins that invoke the Snyk CLI. Successful exploitation of this issue would likely require some level of social engineering - to coerce an untrusted project to be downloaded and analyzed via the Snyk CLI or opened in an IDE where a Snyk IDE plugin is installed and enabled. Additionally, if the IDE has a Trust feature then the target folder must be marked as ‘trusted’ in order to be vulnerable.

NOTE: This issue is independent of the one reported in CVE-2022-40764, and upgrading to a fixed version for this addresses that issue as well.

The affected IDE plugins and versions are:

  • VS Code - Affected: <=1.8.0, Fixed: 1.9.0
  • IntelliJ - Affected: <=2.4.47, Fixed: 2.4.48
  • Visual Studio - Affected: <=1.1.30, Fixed: 1.1.31
  • Eclipse - Affected: <=v20221115.132308, Fixed: All subsequent versions
  • Language Server - Affected: <=v20221109.114426, Fixed: All subsequent versions

🚨 Snyk plugins vulnerable to Command Injection

The package snyk before 1.1064.0; the package snyk-mvn-plugin before 2.31.3; the package snyk-gradle-plugin before 3.24.5; the package @snyk/snyk-cocoapods-plugin before 2.5.3; the package snyk-sbt-plugin before 2.16.2; the package snyk-python-plugin before 1.24.2; the package snyk-docker-plugin before 5.6.5; the package @snyk/snyk-hex-plugin before 1.1.6 are vulnerable to Command Injection due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-40764. A successful exploit allows attackers to run arbitrary commands on the host system where the Snyk CLI is installed by passing in crafted command line flags. In order to exploit this vulnerability, a user would have to execute the snyk test command on untrusted files. In most cases, an attacker positioned to control the command line arguments to the Snyk CLI would already be positioned to execute arbitrary commands. However, this could be abused in specific scenarios, such as continuous integration pipelines, where developers can control the arguments passed to the Snyk CLI to leverage this component as part of a wider attack against an integration/build pipeline. This issue has been addressed in the latest Snyk Docker images available at https://hub.docker.com/r/snyk/snyk as of 2022-11-29. Images downloaded and built prior to that date should be updated. The issue has also been addressed in the Snyk TeamCity CI/CD plugin as of version v20221130.093605.

🚨 Snyk CLI affected by Command Injection vulnerability

Snyk CLI before 1.996.0 allows arbitrary command execution, affecting Snyk IDE plugins and the snyk npm package. Exploitation could follow from the common practice of viewing untrusted files in the Visual Studio Code editor, for example. The original demonstration was with shell metacharacters in the vendor.json ignore field, affecting snyk-go-plugin before 1.19.1. This affects, for example, the Snyk TeamCity plugin (which does not update automatically) before 20220930.142957.

author: chuganzy
body:
_Description of changes:_

This PR aims to fix an issue where the `isSource` property of tokens provided by ES Modules is not updated correctly when running Style Dictionary multiple times with different configurations within the same Node.js process.

This is because Style Dictionary directly mutates the resolved contents during the first run and reuses the value from the second time.

Alternative solution is to just update [`combineJSON`](https://github.com/amzn/style-dictionary/blob/86c2c30ba289121f7dc9c28f573d1996dbc4a3a8/lib/utils/combineJSON.js#L110) to always update the `isSource`, however I thought it makes more sense to clone the original content to make the behavior consistent with other file types. The downside of this approach is that non-serializable data types cannot be used, however I think it is not an issue because Style Dictionary uses `structuredClone` in other places too and does not expect non-serializable data to be put as a token value to begin with.

body:
This pull request introduces a GitHub CLI extension written in Go for repository hydration, including creating demo issues, discussions, and pull requests. It establishes a robust project structure, implements core functionality, and adds tests and CI workflows. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Core Functionality

* Implemented a `hydrate` subcommand to automate repository hydration with demo issues, discussions, and pull requests. It includes options for specifying repository owner, name, and hydration content (`cmd/hydrate.go`, `cmd/root.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-13beda516a753427a6f32c721972e983708f2cce33addde3fd6ae6882b640815L3-R67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ab967ab1a2f3a1b769106eeb7bfe892ef0e81d1d27811fa15be08e6749feee1fL4-R21)
* Added a `GHClient` struct and `GitHubClient` interface to handle GitHub API operations like creating labels, issues, discussions, and PRs (`internal/githubapi/client.go`, `internal/githubapi/interfaces.go`, `internal/githubapi/types.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d5ab40cca51c81771977fcc02ca97175562f82e2b4916052d4c1c022d53ad957R1-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-169f549a85a0a8993a18edace26ec31fb0cbeadfdb947881359705b9d311978dR1-R9) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-80ef40d3cc96334867eada7f78c45a764b7a4cd5fbd3fcd49d17be66c19a19d6R1-R24)
* Created the `hydrate` package to handle hydration logic, including reading JSON files, ensuring labels exist, and collecting labels from issues, discussions, and PRs (`internal/hydrate/hydrate.go`).

### Testing and Validation

* Added unit tests for the `hydrate` package, including tests for hydration logic, JSON parsing, and label management. A mock GitHub client is used to simulate API interactions (`internal/hydrate/hydrate_test.go`).

### Project Setup and Documentation

* Defined project structure and development guidelines in a new documentation file, including coding standards, repository organization, and development workflows (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
* Added demo JSON files for issues, discussions, and pull requests to facilitate hydration (`.github/demos/issues.json`, `.github/demos/discussions.json`, `.github/demos/prs.json`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c917000f82a053f8b7515298b051e02306b951a688543895f30181afddb0a1eeR1-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bcadc43717d80c6940dbbb6d2e303bc0eda02ff6b162e98c521ffd8c0b8dd4eeR1-R8) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b530ace54453b8b183a06dc000022858ae54a5bf1836d058f99ee9a69c7e0d24R1-R10)

### Continuous Integration

* Introduced a GitHub Actions workflow for building, testing, and linting the project on `push` and `pull_request` events targeting the `main` branch (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

### Dependency Management

* Updated `go.mod` to include necessary dependencies such as `spf13/cobra` for CLI commands and `spf13/pflag` for flag parsing (`go.mod`).

author: wpelczar
body:
Fixes #259: Some valid CSP source URLs were rejected.

# What's changed: 
The UrlDomain regular expression was updated. The previous implementation incorrectly rejected several valid sources, including:

- Short domains without schemes (e.g., t.co, x.com).
- URLs with uppercase characters in the path (e.g., https://d1igp3oop3iho5.cloudfront.net/v2/aBC1DeefgH2ij-eu1/zaius-min.js).
- Long subdomain structures like https://aaf1a18515da0e792f78-c27fdabe952dfc357fe25ebf5c8897ee.ssl.cf5.rackcdn.com/....

## Updated Regex 
```csharp
public const string UrlDomain = @"^(?:[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+\-.]*:\/\/)?(?:\*\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+)+|[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+)+|\*)(?::\d+|:\*)?(?:\/[^\s]*)?$";
```

## Regex Breakdown
- `^ ... $`

  - Asserts start and end of the string, ensuring full string match.

- `(?:[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+\-.]*:\/\/)?`

  - Optional scheme, e.g., http://, https://, ws://.

  - Starts with a letter, followed by any combination of letters, digits, `+`, `-`, or `.`.

  - Ends with `://`.

  - Entire group is optional.

- `(?:\*\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+)+ | [a-zA-Z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+)+ | \*)`

- Domain or wildcard:

  - `*.example.com` — Wildcard subdomain (requires at least one dot).

  - `example.com` — Regular domain (requires at least one dot).

  - `* —` Wildcard for any domain.

- `(?::\d+|:\*)?`

  - Optional port:

    - `:443` — Specific numeric port.

    - `:*` — Wildcard port.

- `(?:\/[^\s]*)?`

  - Optional path:

    - `/path/to/resource` — Anything after `/ `except whitespace.
    
 ## Notes
 This updated regex was prepared and validated with the help of **ChatGPT** , based on teh official CSP specification ( [ https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP/#framework-directive-source-list](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP/#framework-directive-source-list))

body:
### Description

This PR extends the number of triggers for the Unsaved Changes alert dialog. It will now be shown not only on `Done` button tap but also on any actions that trigger Modal dismissal. 

In order to do that, I had to update the Compose Unstyled library to have access to the `confirmDetentChange()` callback that was added and does exactly what we need.

Additionally, I had to:
- Remove the custom click handled on the `Scrim`
- Remove the custom `BackHandler`
Those two are now handled by the Modal sheet directly and hence are now routed via `confirmDetentChange` callback that we use. 

On top of that I had to change a bit where we create the `ModalBottomSheetState` as we need it in a certain place for the `confirmDetentChange` callback. 

Now to the actual implementation part: 

I ended up on a Plan B solution - that is to pass down a flag when the user tried to dismiss that dialog. When such a flag is received the `QuickEditorViewModel` will check the page and delegate the unsaved changes check.

Next to the flag we also need a new callback `onDismissIgnored()` to make sure we clear that flag when the user decide to "Keep editing" so that it will be possible to send it again later.

author: atsampson
body:
In older versions of C, `void foo()` declares a function that can take any set of arguments. In C23, `()` means the same as `(void)`: the function takes no arguments.

`elk.h` declares many functions with `()`, so function arguments weren't being checked. Compiling with GCC 15, which uses C23 by default, revealed some cases where functions were being prototyped or called with incorrect arguments.

body:
Friends page now displays the users received friend requests, friends list, and other users they can send a friend request to. 

Users can click a button to send a friend request, and can then cancel the request if they wish. 

The other user will receive the request, and it will show under their pending requests. They can either accept the request, and the friend will go to their friends list, or they can decline, where they will go to the list of users they can send friend requests to. 

A user can also remove a friend from their friends list. 

Currently the Send Friend Request heading shows all registered users who are not any of the following: 
- Already friends with the current user (shown under friends list)
- Have already sent a friend request to the current user (request is pending)
- The current user (cannot send friend request to self)

Could implement a search feature in future so user can search a list of users by username, especially if the user base expanded. Additionally, the UI design of the friends page is basic, but will update it once the profile updates have been completed, as will need to show the profile icons rather than placeholders.
